features.title: Classic workspace
features.scope: Classic stage, tools, timeline, Library, Properties, Actions, Accessibility, Output, Align, Transform, Color, Swatches, Info, Ease, History, Scene, Motion editor and Project panels with Light/Dark themes. Dockable panels share a four-sided configurable dock grid with resizable areas/groups, ordered tabs and native floating windows. Header drag supports docking, tab merging/reordering, splits and undocking. Saved workspace geometry is separate from document content. Actions provides frame/object/source editing and source-specific feedback. Info edits selection W/H/X/Y as one Undo step and shows live cursor coordinates in ruler units plus RGBA color under the stage pointer. Shared label/value rows and compact system fonts align controls across panels; the Library preview stays above the scrolling browser. Panels move between native windows; floating windows retain their own tab groups and horizontal/vertical split trees. Escape and source-window closure cancel an active drag. Dedicated boundary grips resize dock areas, including Timeline height; menu shortcuts use separate aligned columns. Individual tabs and complete tab groups have distinct drag handles. Floating Edit/Dock commands live in the compact header menu. Numeric controls support click/type and drag/scrub. Properties separates selection and tool contexts with collapsible sections and paired fields; Library keeps search and commands fixed around one scrolling list. Native palettes are bundled from the shared design tokens. All panels use the common control density and semantic themes, bounded menus with aligned shortcuts, and explicit overflow controls. Fresh compact workspaces group Library and Properties without replacing saved custom layouts. View ▸ Rulers / Grid / Guides, zoom-control toggles and the Rulers, guides & grid popover share one setting state; Save as default stores it in the editor preferences. The Stage shows NF2 tool and handle cursors and NF2 selection/transform boxes, anchors and marquee in both themes.
features.limitations: Main-window side groups remain stacked rows/columns; arbitrary recursive main-window splits, named workspace presets and multiple open documents remain unfinished. VoiceOver/IME and mixed-DPI monitors need broader platform acceptance.

features.title: Free Transform
features.scope: Move, scale and rotate individual objects; uniformly scale and rotate a group through stage gestures. Transform panel adds exact position/dimensions, optional linked proportions and nonuniform W/H scaling of the selection, plus single-object rotation/skew, flips and reset. Skew-aware handle resizing preserves its fixed anchor and authored reflection. Free Transform uses the NF2 transform box with Flash zones and a draggable transformation point (`Transform.pivot` in format 7 for single placements and a transient stage pivot for multi-selections; rotation and ⌥-scale pivot around it, double-click resets to centre): handles scale, edges skew, just outside a corner rotates, inside moves; NF2 cursors show each zone.
features.limitations: The transform box is axis-aligned for rotated objects (NF2 request R-011), and direct numeric skew editing of multi-object groups remains unfinished. Numeric selection sizing and stage transform gestures have separate supported operations.

features.title: Library and nested editing
features.scope: Reusable instances and nested editing preserve authored identity and scripts. Convert to Symbol offers aligned name/type/folder, nine-point registration and export identifier/existing-class fields. The Library shows a real first-frame preview, persistent folders, inline organization, search by name/path/linkage/class, Name/Type/Linkage sorting and visible linkage. Duplicate symbol clones non-scene symbols with fresh IDs and cleared linkage; Delete symbol removes the symbol and cleans up any placed instances across timelines in one Undo step; Swap symbol in the Library replaces selected stage instances' symbol while preserving transform, name, scripts and compatible playback. Folder paths survive symbol clipboard transfers; conflicts reject before mutation. Empty symbol creation opens nested editing. Buttons expose Up/Over/Down/Hit, instance actions and authored/export-linked SimpleButton typing. Library Properties changes kind across references while preserving keys/scripts and refusing incompatible class linkage.
features.limitations: Properties Swap… picker and Stage context-menu Swap/Duplicate symbol… wait for NF2 request R-012. Arbitrary runtime state-object assignment, empty SimpleButton construction, 9-slice guides and legacy shared libraries remain unsupported. Multi-object conversion requires a contiguous stack on one layer. Preview is the first frame; folder organization uses controls, not drag-and-drop. Resource files remain outside the symbol-folder tree.

features.title: Authored text
features.scope: Editable authored TextBox with logical dimensions, multiline/wrapping, installed regular/bold/italic fonts, size/color/leading and left/center/right alignment. Old unboxed Text retains its appearance until explicit conversion. AS3 TextField/TextFormat and AS2 createTextField share Rust state and line layout, with separate current/insertion formats and bounded whole-field/string editing. Scripted HTML5 input adds native browser editing, Rust revision-checked user transactions, UTF-16 selection/replacement, user-only restrict/maxChars and password masking. AS3 TextFieldType/TextEvent/FocusEvent and AS2 Selection/onChanged/focus callbacks share Stage focus and publication lifetime.
features.limitations: Mixed character runs, HTML/CSS, auto-size, advanced paragraphs and full shaping/Flash metrics remain pending. Host font measurements may produce different line breaks and pixels; portable fonts are separate work. Native headless layout/clipping/Undo and in-app-browser reflow/alignment, independent fields and Restart passed. Native interactive editing remains pending; VERIFICATION.md preserves the exact scope separately from earlier plain-text evidence. Independent fba17ae evidence (TEXT-LAYOUT-HTML5-20261027T0409Z) covers only the actual uniform layout/format/refusal/Restart workflow in VERIFICATION.md. Native live editing, other fonts/engines, mixed runs and input/IME do not inherit the browser pass. The separate text-form delivery records current scripted input evidence; earlier layout evidence is unchanged. The active DOM field follows affine/vector clipping but is above foreground Canvas artwork. Native input-field authoring, full IME/locale/grapheme/original-player behavior, rich text and cross-engine metrics remain pending; AS2 general string target resolution is unsupported.

features.title: Gradients, masks and effects
features.scope: Authored vector masks, Color panel Linear/Radial gradient creation and stop editing, Swatches panel (`Window ▸ Swatches` `⌘F9` and Color panel ⋯ `Add swatch`) and Gradient Transform. The Color panel switches fill and stroke paints between None, Solid colour, Linear gradient and Radial gradient (converting solid shapes to `PaintedPath` while preserving parametric geometry) and edits stops on `NF2/Gradient Bar` with `NF2/Color Picker`. Gradient Transform moves, scales and rotates gradient fills on Stage. Scripted HTML5 filters add copied Blur/Glow/DropShadow/ColorMatrix values, shared bounded Rust RGBA kernels and ordered whole-subtree groups, including nested effects and deferred owner mask/scroll clipping. Runtime BitmapData image processing adds color/filter operations and current subtree capture through the shared scene painter; AS3 adds bulk ByteArray transfer and PNG encoding with Loader round-trip. Authored vector mask layers now clip native stage meshes and HTML5 draws using shared Rust geometry; vector-only nested symbols are supported as mask sources. Show Masking exposes the editable source, and clipping is applied to stage picking.
features.limitations: Scripted HTML5 Graphics supports bounded linear/radial gradients and vector display masks. Gradient Flow Reflect/Repeat and Linear RGB interpolation, radial focal handles on Stage, project-file swatch persistence (current user-added swatches live in workspace prefs alongside derived document paints), Properties Colour effect style rows (Brightness/Tint/Advanced, R-012), filter authoring, bitmap fills and alpha masks remain pending; runtime support does not complete these authoring operations. This runtime-only filter profile has its own gallery evidence; native filter authoring, remaining classes, exact Flash kernels/coercions and high-density raster fidelity remain pending. Active native DOM editing under a filtered ancestor is an explicit composition boundary. Original geometry supplies input and semantics; effect halos do not extend them. Independent 5395375 evidence (FILTERS-HTML5-20261027T0844Z) confirms only the scripted filter-gallery publication and common browser regression. Runtime pixels and input do not complete native effect authoring, exact Flash kernels or filtered-input composition. The image pipeline remains bounded: normal draw blending, integer regions, no external mask dependencies, no display filters during draw, partial setPixels underrun, and separate native authoring/exact raster acceptance. Authored text/bitmap mask sources and masks nested inside mask sources diagnose; native mask preview has a bounded complexity limit.

features.title: Layer organization
features.scope: Compact left-aligned layer names with row dividers and inline rename. Layer context menus provide visibility/locks, insert/delete, document-local copy/cut/paste/duplicate, merge and layer/group-to-symbol conversion. Folders support child grouping, collapse, inherited visibility/locks and editable properties. Guides remain authoring-only; mask relationships use stable layer IDs. Per-layer colored squares toggle authoring outlines; an RGB dialog edits the saved outline color with one Undo. Outlined folders include descendants within the edited symbol; nested symbol outline preferences do not leak into parent artwork. Native transport and publication retain original fills and strokes. Layer-column width is draggable and saved as a workspace preference. Name dragging reorders a layer or its dependent folder/mask group with insertion feedback, cancellation and one Undo. Upper sibling rows represent foreground layers; drag reordering and frame paste follow the visible order without reversing the serialized painter order. Add motion guide inserts "Guide: <name>" above a layer and guides it; classic tweens on the guided layer move along the guide's first stroke in the editor and HTML5, and the guide is never published.
features.limitations: Orient to path turns guided objects in the editor and HTML5 but has no Properties control yet; arbitrary multi-row selection and drag-to-reparent remain unfinished. Reordering preserves existing parent/mask IDs. Layer clipboard stays within the current document. Merging tweened layers samples frames into keys.

features.title: Keyframes, blank frames and holds
features.scope: F5/F6/F7 and moving/copying individual keyframes; insertion uses the visible interpolated pose. Held content and blank spans are drawn to the next chronological key or symbol end. Frame rows are separated from scrollbars; key dragging uses the original pressed frame, a destination preview and edge scrolling. Frame zoom and Fit change cell width with adaptive ruler labels and selected-frame recentering, without changing authored timing. Compact FPS and total-duration fields preserve frame count and set the nearest integer FPS when duration changes.
features.limitations: The last key holds content to the explicit layer end or symbol end. Blank keys stop visible content earlier. Range operations and their tween-baking boundaries are tracked separately.

features.title: Graphic synchronization
features.scope: Graphic supports loop, play-once and single-frame modes relative to the authored timeline. Loop and Play once accept a placement-specific First frame; Single frame retains its direct frame selector. Synchronise symbols (frame menu, Edit / Modify ▸ Timeline) sets the first frame of graphic instances on the selected keyframes so their nested animation continues from the previous keyframe.
features.limitations: Exact compatibility with every mode in source Flash projects requires separate fixtures.

features.title: Pose interpolation
features.scope: Tweens match stable object identities and interpolate position, scale, rotation, alpha and supported geometry/color properties. Format 5 also interpolates affine skew and color transforms, with classic Flash acceleration and single global cubic easing. Motion tweens (blue spans) target one symbol instance or text block: editing it inside the span creates a ◆ property keyframe that keys exactly the changed properties, F6 keys all of them, and each property interpolates on its own track with the span ease. Removing the tween drops its ◆ keys; switching to classic keeps their poses as keyframes. The selected motion-tweened instance shows its path on the stage with a dot per frame and ◆ key points; dragging a point moves that key (keys X and Y) with one Undo. The Motion editor shows each property track over the span, adds or removes one property's ◆ key at the playhead, edits values and jumps between keys; Properties — Motion tween edits the span ease, rotation turns and direction, Orient to path and the path box. Copy motion records the classic or motion tween under the playhead; Paste motion animates the selected object the same way relative to its own pose.
features.limitations: Per-property eases, Sync graphic symbols, Snap to motion guide and moving keys in time inside the Motion editor are missing. Paste motion special has no dialog design yet (R-006). The path is edited only at its key points (no Bézier path editing).

features.title: Easing and custom curves
features.scope: Keyframe Properties selects Linear, EaseIn/Out/InOut, a custom cubic Bézier curve with four numeric control coordinates (Y may overshoot) or Flash acceleration (−100…100). The Ease panel edits the curve of the tween under the playhead (classic, shape or motion) with presets including Back, draggable Bézier handles, a preview track and Apply/Cancel as one Undo step. The shared model also preserves classic Flash acceleration from imported timelines. Scripted HTML5 easing/Tween uses a separate Rust family for built-in curves and bounded frame-based or seconds-based animation.
features.limitations: Independent property curves remain unfinished. Bounce and Elastic are not single cubic curves and stay disabled in the Ease panel. Runtime Tween retains built-in easing identities and finite positive durations; complete Flash timing and curve conformance are not claimed.

features.title: Shape morphing
features.scope: Shape tweens are a span kind (green) created from the Timeline controls, frame menu and Insert menu. Shapes pair by identity, then by order; rectangles, ovals and paths morph in parent space. Matching command structure interpolates exactly; different contours are resampled by arc length with start-point alignment. Fills, strokes and compatible gradients interpolate. Unpaired shapes and contours shrink or grow from their centre. Evaluation is shared by the editor and HTML5.
features.limitations: Shape hints are missing. Contours pair by index, so very different contour counts or holes can morph unnaturally. Symbols, text and bitmaps on a shape-tweened layer hold still. Gradients of different kind or stop count switch at the midpoint.

features.title: Frame-range operations
features.scope: Rectangular multi-layer selection; copy, cut, paste, move, clear, insert and remove time as atomic Undo operations. Explicit Include frame scripts transfers symbol-level code once and rejects destination collisions; object scripts travel with placements. Independent layer ends can be set numerically or dragged and stop exposure in native and HTML5 evaluation. macOS range clipboard and visible layer-order paste are supported.
features.limitations: Creation of destination layer structure remain unfinished. Frame clips are session-local and require existing destination rows. Trimming deletes later keys with Undo recovery. Edits intersecting tweens bake the touched segment to integer-frame poses instead of retaining editable sliced easing curves. Edit multiple frames shows every keyframe in the onion range and moves the selected objects on all of them; other edits still apply to the current keyframe. Reversing a motion tween turns its ◆ poses into classic keyframes.

features.title: Complete Flash timeline lifecycle
features.scope: Removing and recreating an instance starts a new lifetime; stale dispatches are rejected and goto has protection against an unbounded queue. Same-path symbol replacement resets subtree overrides, custom fields and clocks, invalidates old proxies and preserves siblings; accepted in Chrome/in-app HTML5.
features.limitations: Construction/re-entry order, complex nested goto and complete Flash Player semantics still need conformance work.

features.title: Audio and video synchronization
features.scope: Timeline sound with Event/Start/Stop/Stream sync, repeat/loop and preset effects in editor playback and HTML5, coordinated stream stops and seeks; timeline video.
features.limitations: Timeline video, custom sound envelopes, Sound properties export settings and decoded waveform display are not implemented. Streams are not re-synchronised when a host drops frames, and editor scrubbing is silent. HTML5 timeline sound needs Enable audio and plays MP3/WAV.

features.title: Shared Rust/WASM core
features.scope: The browser uses the same timeline runtime; tests call the actual compiled WASM. Runtime-created object identity, hierarchy, solid drawing, transformed bounds/hits and captured lifecycle routes use the shared Rust/WASM scene while authored documents remain immutable. Explicit linked MovieClip namespaces reuse the shared timeline evaluator with independent frame scripts, nested clocks and ref-based semantic targets, including detached playback. Bounded AMF0/AMF3 values are encoded/decoded in Rust and used by ByteArray object records and local AS2/AS3 SharedObject persistence. The second bounded runtime batch adds Rust date/number formatting, four rendered filter families and manual AS3 event payload classes.
features.limitations: A shared implementation does not prove compatibility with Flash behavior. The combined dynamic-display browser workflow and Restart passed; authored/dynamic reordering and full Flash construction order remain bounded. Independent 2b5deff evidence covers only the exact dynamic drawing/identity or binary packet scenarios in VERIFICATION.md; other members and native error/coercion fidelity remain unverified. Independent 798e28b evidence (LINKED-INTERFACES-HTML5-20261027T0243Z) applies only to the linked timeline and interface/accessor observations in VERIFICATION.md. AS2 host-error catch recovery, complete construction order and uncalled members remain unverified or outside the supported profile. This persistence/codec delivery has separate evidence. Typed aliases/class reconstruction, externalizable/XML/Vector/Dictionary values, native .sol files and remote synchronization remain pending. Browser quota/access and HTTP(S) origin rules apply; Restart discards unflushed edits. AMF payload size excludes the storage envelope and historical filesystem overhead.

features.title: Authored events and interactivity
features.scope: Authored frame/Load/Click/EnterFrame handlers plus shared display/Stage EventDispatcher subscriptions, propagation/cancellation, bounded keyboard/pointer input and AS2 onEnterFrame/onPress callbacks. Captured AS2 Key/Mouse/Stage listener objects, keyboard state and hook-based cursor visibility share the same input hub and reset lifecycle. Publication-owned AS3 timers drive the same script/render lifecycle, with completion, elapsed-time queries and Restart cleanup; the geometry-timer example combines this with typed affine geometry and live text. Pointer capture and outside release share the drag lifecycle; AS2 gains onRelease/onReleaseOutside/onRollOver/onRollOut, and mouse target flags/cursor preferences are resolved against the current Rust display graph. Rust-owned callback timer IDs add AS2/AS3 interval/timeout functions; the scripted Tween family shares the existing event/scheduler service. Bounded AS2 AsBroadcaster adds ordered listener identity, dispatch and publication reset cleanup. The second bounded runtime batch adds Rust date/number formatting, four rendered filter families and manual AS3 event payload classes.
features.limitations: Full Flash construction/event order, remaining native callbacks, fullscreen/IME/touch and complete owner-specific API guards remain unfinished. Representative family behavior passed in the shared in-app-browser batch; this is not full API or cross-engine acceptance. Independent frozen-01f1381 browser verification found trusted mouse click events with isPrimary=false dropped by the shared Stage guard; semantic Enter and keyboard paths passed. The corrected input route passed coordinate clicks and Restart in the original class/Stage examples; an unlocated aggregate observer exception remains open. The new AS2 combined scenario has executable host/WASM evidence; representative coordinate clicks, keyboard and Restart also passed in the in-app browser. The combined geometry/Timer browser workflow and Restart passed; historical Flash timing and cross-engine conformance remain unverified. Independent a3fedc3 browser evidence covers the specific class/input scenarios in VERIFICATION.md; all untested members remain bounded or unverified. This family has separate grouped input/drag verification; exact historical event ordering, all native-text/semantic combinations, multi-touch and other browser engines remain unverified. The drag delivery separately passed real AS2/AS3 browser drags, invisible donor margin, child/disabled targeting, outside release and fresh Restart callbacks; existing linked-card Canvas and keyboard activation also passed. Native capture-at-Restart and cursor values retain controlled-helper evidence. Full declaration promotion remains a separate audit. Independent 01f2261 evidence (POINTER-HTML5-20261027T1113Z) is restricted to the real drag/drop, child/disabled targeting, outside-release and Restart observations in VERIFICATION.md. The actual AS3 parent is unrotated and AS2 parent is −4 degrees, both scale 1. Cursor effects, active-capture Restart, lockCenter, active bounds mutation, arbitrary donor/transform/cancellation cases and every nested hit path were not independently accepted. The linked regression has successful body/key controls plus one unresolved first coordinate miss; it is not complete nested-target coverage. The shared linked body/semantic controls preserve authored behavior in the tested routes, while the first possible nested-badge miss remains unresolved. Native cursor/accessibility conformance is not inferred. Callback timer/Tween/broadcaster behavior is partial, and the newly added broadcaster browser scenario is pending. Historical event order, arbitrary coercion and direct listener-array mutation are not claimed. This hour's batch remains partial; acceptance and any observed failures are recorded separately in docs/AS-RUNTIME-HOUR.md. Earlier browser evidence does not certify the new entries or full historical conformance.

features.scope: Embedded AS2/AS3 source units use distinct bounded class profiles with exact imports, shared publication programs, authored symbol linkage and source-path diagnostics. AS2 root document linkage is a NeoFlash extension. Sources can be browsed, created, renamed, deleted and published from the Project panel (showing class linkage to symbols or the document class, with double-click opening Actions) and edited in Actions. Actions offers a toolbox and code hints generated from the declarations NeoFlash implements or partially implements, plus project classes scanned from source, a Script navigator, auto-indent formatting, comment commands and a silent live check. AS3 projects can import bounded ByteArray/Endian buffers; unsupported native inheritance and constructor forms produce source diagnostics. Explicit exported MovieClip classes instantiate shared library timelines through AS3 construction or AS2 attachMovie, with independent namespace refs, nested clocks and script targets. Public AS3 get/set accessors and project interface contracts share the existing source compiler. Portable project resources feed the AS3 URLRequest/URLLoader/URLVariables and AS2 LoadVars families; requests share publication lifecycle and binary/event services. AS3 lexical class access, final/dynamic declarations and package wildcards connect encapsulated models to public data/display APIs; AS2 retains distinct compile-time private rules. The bounded AS2/AS3 hour adds and migrates large runtime families through the existing compiler and HTML5 exporter: Math (19 migrated paths), geometry/Color (74 migrated and 46 new entries), strings/codecs (19 migrated and 8 new), easing/Tween/CustomEase/timers (121 new), ByteArray codecs (5 migrated and 12 new), and AsBroadcaster (5 new). Individual licensed algorithms are adapted into the shared Rust core; browser adapters bind object identity, callbacks and browser facilities. Shared aliases and reused kernels are counted separately from algorithms; no editor, FLA or full-VM completion is implied.
features.limitations: JS/TS modules, SWC dependencies, complete type checking, compiler-backed completion (current hints are lexical), warnings/quick fixes, debugger/source maps and full class semantics remain pending. Representative linked-class behavior and Restart passed in the shared in-app-browser batch; native Sources acceptance remains pending. The AS2 combined export/WASM/input scenario passes; representative coordinate clicks, keyboard and Restart also passed in the in-app browser. Bounded binary-buffer workflow has independent browser evidence on 2b5deff; binary memory support does not imply loaders, external IO or resource-document support. Independent 2b5deff evidence covers only the exact dynamic drawing/identity or binary packet scenarios in VERIFICATION.md; other members and native error/coercion fidelity remain unverified. Linked MovieClip and accessor/interface workflows passed the shared in-app-browser batch; native Export identifier editing remains pending. Independent 798e28b evidence (LINKED-INTERFACES-HTML5-20261027T0243Z) applies only to the linked timeline and interface/accessor observations in VERIFICATION.md. AS2 host-error catch recovery, complete construction order and uncalled members remain unverified or outside the supported profile. Independent c39a29e acceptance (RESOURCES-HTML5-20261027T0323Z) covers the precise embedded/HTTP and pending-request observations in VERIFICATION.md; native resource authoring and full network semantics remain unverified. These are delivery-batch entry counts, not a complete declaration audit or language-compatibility percentage. Broader product work remains paused; the hour report records executed export/browser evidence and unresolved failures. This hour's batch remains partial; acceptance and any observed failures are recorded separately in docs/AS-RUNTIME-HOUR.md. Earlier browser evidence does not certify the new entries or full historical conformance.

features.title: Image, audio and video assets
features.scope: Library imports and stores portable resource files, including image/audio/video bytes, with metadata editing, Undo and self-contained HTML5 packaging. The shared data service loads embedded text, bytes and form variables and supports bounded HTTP(S) requests. PNG/JPEG resources can be placed on Stage with transforms and smoothing. Shared Rust BitmapData buffers support bounded pixel edits, fill/copy/clone/scroll and disposal; AS3 Bitmap and AS2 attachBitmap use the same display graph and publication lifetime. AS3 Sound/SoundChannel/SoundTransform and AS2 Sound add complete-file MP3/WAV resource/HTTP loading, gesture-enabled playback, stop/repeats, volume/pan and completion callbacks. AS3 Loader/LoaderInfo and AS2 MovieClipLoader now connect encoded PNG/JPEG resource/HTTP bytes to managed display content and the Rust pixel arena. Runtime BitmapData image processing adds color/filter operations and current subtree capture through the shared scene painter; AS3 adds bulk ByteArray transfer and PNG encoding with Loader round-trip. Authored/dynamic Video display leaves, native placeholder insertion and browser NetStream file playback use the shared scene graph and portable resources; HTTP media uses native browser CORS transport. SVG/PNG/JPEG Stage import shares a menu/file-drop path, creates library symbols, reuses identical resources and commits multi-file batches as one Undo. Solid SVG paths stay editable; richer paint renders through Rust resvg with original SVG retention. Native file-drop coordinates, page fitting and visible-layer fallback keep imported graphics on Stage. Library symbols and supported stored image resources can also be dragged or placed through the same transaction.
features.limitations: Additional image formats, bitmap fills, remaining filter/draw/encoding operations, sound streaming, native video decoding/synchronization and font embedding remain planned. Audio uses a bounded browser playback service; its own verification is recorded separately. Native resource/image panel acceptance and direct-file browser opening remain pending. The bitmap workflow passed combined export/WASM and in-app-browser observation of shared edits, independent source/clone, AS2 attachment and Restart. Full bitmap conformance is not established; exact evidence is in VERIFICATION.md. Independent c39a29e acceptance (RESOURCES-HTML5-20261027T0323Z) covers the precise embedded/HTTP and pending-request observations in VERIFICATION.md; native resource authoring and full network semantics remain unverified. Independent 1bd0e3c evidence (BITMAP-HTML5-20261027T0345Z) is restricted to the PNG/shared pixel, AS2 attachment, disposal and Restart observations in VERIFICATION.md. JPEG, rasterization options, alpha hits and native image authoring do not inherit that pass. The separate Sound delivery verifies ordinary AS2/AS3 MP3 loading, silent Play/Stop/Restart and actual browser MP3/offline PCM/native lifecycle; WAV native decoding, other engines and audible quality remain unverified. Independent d8f580a evidence (AUDIO-HTML5-20261027T0429Z) covers only the embedded-AS3/HTTP-AS2 original-MP3 workflow, silent native completion with bounded repeats, transform copy/refusal, active Stop and publication Restart in VERIFICATION.md. It does not inherit the separate main-delivery offline PCM probe or establish audible quality, native WAV decoding, nonzero offsets/gain, full mixer semantics or pending-decode races. Image loading excludes SWF/GIF, application/security domains, native Loader subclasses and general legacy target addressing. Retained AS3 content survives unload; explicit disposal/Restart and shared arena limits apply while full garbage collection remains pending. The loader-gallery delivery has separate evidence; previous resource/bitmap audits do not promote new loader declarations. The image pipeline remains bounded: normal draw blending, integer regions, no external mask dependencies, no display filters during draw, partial setPixels underrun, and separate native authoring/exact raster acceptance. Native Video insertion/Properties has separate UI acceptance from compile/model checks. Full media timeline synchronization, capture/publishing and legacy video codecs remain open. The Video delivery separately passed one actual-browser AS2/AS3 MP4 workflow: metadata, changing pixels, paused-frame retention, seek/resume/completion, Close retention, local HTTP playback and Restart. The tiny silent fixture does not establish progressive-before-download completion, audible quality, other codecs/engines or native authoring UI. Independent f42ad94 evidence (VIDEO-HTML5-20261027T1042Z) covers the observed embedded AS3/AS2 four-second MP4, native metadata/status/pixels, pause/seek/resume/natural completion, post-completion Close retention, AS3-only clear and active AS2 HTTP Restart/fresh playback in VERIFICATION.md. The negative AS3 seek preserves time; the unsupported-pan diagnostic does not implement panning. Configured volume zero and silent AAC are not audible-effect evidence. Active/pending close, arbitrary rebinding/reentry, smoothing comparisons, other codecs, large progressive/range/CORS transport, exact synchronization and native Video authoring do not inherit this pass. SVG scripts, animation, external file references and embedded HTML reject. Complex SVG paint is an image after import; original source remains available.

features.scope: Format detection, bounded ZIP/CFB readers, path/size/integrity checks and explicit refusal without overwriting the source. features.title: Binary FLA to editable document
features.scope: Native conversion for Flash 3, 5, MX, 8, CS3 and CS4 preserves scenes, library folders and symbols, ordered layers with masks, folders and motion guides, held keys, nested instances with graphic first-frame offsets, classic and shape tweens with easing, text, PNG bitmaps, uncompressed PCM (`audio/wav`) and MP3 (`audio/mpeg`) sound resources, `CPicFrame` timeline frame sounds (`Event`/`Start`/`Stop`/`Stream` sync, repeats/loop-forever and preset effects) and ActionScript (legacy Actions-panel commands translated to AS1). Features the model cannot express yet are approximated or kept as visible placeholders, each with a located warning; the original FLA is embedded in parts when it fits, and oversized documents fit within the 128 MiB project JSON budget by shedding largest media first, compacting provenance placement tables and degrading excess later vector paths to placeholders with warnings. 105 of 106 local documents import (every non-empty file) and every one round-trips save/reopen unchanged.
features.limitations: Filters, blend modes, 3D, compressed legacy audio codecs (ADPCM/GSM/Nellymoser), custom multi-point sound envelopes/trim points, video, dynamic/input and rich text styling, motion-object/IK animation and component behavior are approximated with warnings. Documents whose converted media and geometry exceed the 128 MiB project JSON limit shed oversized media or later vector paths to placeholders rather than streaming unbounded assets. Font metrics may differ; output is not claimed pixel-identical to Flash.

features.title: Independent project format
features.scope: Versioned JSON stores stable symbols/placements/frames/scripts; version 2 adds logical project source units and document/symbol linkage with path, size and reference validation. Existing version-1 projects remain supported. Version 3 adds portable resource bytes, normalized logical paths/types, strict base64/size validation and shared immutable storage across native snapshots; versions 1 and 2 remain readable. Authored Bitmap elements reference portable PNG/JPEG resource IDs with validated intrinsic dimensions; mutable runtime pixels stay outside the document. TextBox stores explicit layout dimensions and uniform formatting; legacy Text remains readable without conversion, and runtime insertion defaults stay outside authored state. Format 4 adds authored layer roles/relationships and logical library folders with backward-compatible defaults. Format 5 adds affine skew, inherited color transforms, authored gradient paths, Flash easing and an explicit AS1 script identity. Format 6 adds multi-scene lists, tween kinds, motion property keys, motion and ruler guides and frame sounds. Format 7 adds parametric rectangle corner radii, oval start/end angles, inner radius and close-path options (`Transform.primitive`) and custom transform pivots (`Transform.pivot`). Modify ▸ Document… (⌘J) edits stage size, Match contents, anchored content scaling, units, background and frame rate in one Undo step and saves new-document defaults in workspace prefs.
features.limitations: Additional media consumers, embedded font layout and broader asset dependency authoring remain separate work. Independent c39a29e acceptance (RESOURCES-HTML5-20261027T0323Z) covers the precise embedded/HTTP and pending-request observations in VERIFICATION.md; native resource authoring and full network semantics remain unverified. Independent 1bd0e3c evidence (BITMAP-HTML5-20261027T0345Z) is restricted to the PNG/shared pixel, AS2 attachment, disposal and Restart observations in VERIFICATION.md. JPEG, rasterization options, alpha hits and native image authoring do not inherit that pass.
